newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean Kim's top aide summoned over Hanbo scandal.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean Kim's top aide summoned over Hanbo scandal.

text.p: South Korean state prosecutors have summoned three politicians, including a close associate of President Kim Young-sam, in connection with controversial loans to Hanbo Steel Co, prosecution officials said on Monday.

They said Hong In-gil, a member of parliament of Kim's ruling New Korea Party and until last year a top official at the presidential Blue House, was asked to appear at the prosecution office by 2.00 p.m. (0500 GMT) on Monday.
Kim, who ordered a probe into the loans last month, has called the scandal a typical example of corruption.
Also summoned by prosecutors is Kwon Roh-kap, a prominent opposition member of parliament and a top aide to opposition leader Kim Dae-jung. The other politician was not identified.

The three were the first politicians to be probed over loans totalling five trillion won ($5.8 billion) provided to Hanbo Steel, South Korea's second largest steelmaker, before it was declared insolvent on January 23.
"Prosecutors will try to find out whether banks had granted loans under pressure," a prosecution official told Reuters.
Prosecutors have arrested Chung Tae-soo, founder of the Hanbo Group and its steelmaking flagship, and two leading bankers over the loan scandal.
Chung has been charged with fraud and other violations while the bankers were accused of taking 400 million won each from Chung in return for offering loans to Hanbo.

Hong, who has been Kim's close associate for more than two decades, has denied taking money from Hanbo while Kwon admitted last week to accepting between 150 million and 160 million won from Chung, partly to fund an election campaign.

Kwon, a leading member of the main opposition National Congress for New Politics, said he had nothing to do with Hanbo loans and that he believed the money was either "political funds or rice cake money".
South Koreans traditionally swap small amounts of money, known as rice cake money, or gifts during major holidays as a token of friendship or respect.

National Congress has accused the government of peddling influence for the massive loans that allowed Hanbo to emerge as South Korea's 14th largest conglomerate by rapidly expanding the steelmaking flagship and by acquiring or setting up 18 companies over the past three years.
Political analysts said with only 10 months away from presidential elections, the Hanbo scandal could have a serious impact on the polls.

The president has worked hard to build a reputation as an anti-graft crusader since he took office in 1993 but his image was hurt in the past year when several of his top officials, including a defence minister, were arrested on bribery charges.
